items.summary: A year ago, NVIDIA open sourced its Aerial wireless software alongside Sionna and other tools aimed at accelerating next-generation 6G network development. Global developer adoption of the AI Aerial and Sionna software has grown 10x over the past year, while the broader toolset surpassed 1 million downloads; more than 8,000 research and academic institutions worldwide now use them. Researchers report a robot task completion time reduction of up to 52.6% versus periodic images at King’s College London, higher uplink throughput for SoftBank’s neural receiver across all tested settings, and a RAN power consumption cut of 45.6% from the University of Leeds team.
items.title: NVIDIA Open Source Tools Advance 6G Research

items.summary: Google's Data Cloud connectors, now in preview within Gemini, let business users and analysts query live enterprise data using natural language. The feature addresses a common problem: across most organizations, data questions multiply faster than analysts can answer them, stalling projects and spreading unmanaged spreadsheets. Early generative AI tools struggled with accurate SQL generation and governance rules; these connectors resolve governed data directly from the workspace while enforcing row- and column-level security under end-user credentials. Queries run through Knowledge Catalog to map everyday terms into exact database structures, then execute via permission-aware execution using federated query mode without copying or indexing data.
items.title: Data Cloud Connectors Bring Conversational Analytics to Gemini in Preview

items.summary:
A new Ramp report finds that although companies are using more AI than ever, their spending on it has flatlined over late summer even as token volumes rose. According to Ramp's data, token spend grew only 1. 5% across August and September, compared with 42% in July. Ramp lead economist Ara Kharazian told TechCrunch that almost all AI spend comes from venture-backed tech firms, so a slowdown among the top cohort could trigger cascading effects despite rising volumes. He attributes the trend to price cuts by OpenAI and Anthropic and growing customer thriftiness rather than weak demand. The report arrives as Bloomberg reported Anthropic's potential valuation fell sharply before its IPO. Kharazian cautioned that assumptions about sustained hypergrowth may be breaking down, though he noted a re-acceleration in October data remains possible.

items.title: Ramp Data Signals AI Spending Slowdown Ahead of Anthropic IPO

items.summary: A November roundup reports job cuts at several large tech firms just before the holiday season. The companies named are Amazon, Angi, Block, Canva, and Squarespace. For Amazon specifically, a Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notice filed with Washington state indicates about 95 employees will be separated from employment in the state; Amazon described this as “approximately 95 employees will be separated from employment with Amazon.” The notice lists affected roles including managers, software developers, engineers, and more. These WARN layoffs follow workers notified in October, adding to over 30,000 Amazon layoffs in the past year.
items.title: Tech Layoffs Hit Amazon, Angi, Block, Canva and Squarespace Before Holidays

items.summary: ZDNET reports that Apple will begin monitoring public iCloud links for harmful content starting with iOS 27.3, affecting only links marked “Anyone with the Link.” The company says it may block or disable accounts and involve law enforcement if policy is violated, but did not define what constitutes harmful content. Limited-access links remain encrypted and unmonitored. Apple also notes an appeals framework exists for false flags.
items.title: Apple Begins Monitoring Public iCloud Links in iOS 27.3

items.summary: On Friday, Amazon announced a new feature letting customers chat with its Alexa AI agent over text messages to shop on the platform. The rollout targets select U.S. customers just before holiday shopping begins and can be expanded in coming weeks via waitlist signups. Users may search, add items to cart, purchase, compare products, upload images for similar listings, track prices, manage lists, and check order status.
items.title: Amazon launches text-based Alexa shopping feature ahead of holidays

items.summary: Veeam warned customers that its Software Appliance virtual machines can intermittently fail to boot and crash with a kernel panic after rebooting, including reboots following updates. The company said the issue stems from an early-boot FIPS-mode jitterentropy health test in the appliance's Linux kernel failing on certain AMD EPYC processors, such as 7262, 7302, and 7F72. Veeam noted affected systems show a specific kernel panic error message. It advised redeploying to an unaffected processor or disabling automatic updates.
items.title: Veeam Warns of Boot Failures on AMD EPYC Hosts

items.summary: In The Blueprint, Mito's CEO Iñaki Berenguer and Head of Engineering Keyvan Akbary describe building an orchestration platform on Google Cloud to produce a 120-second national TV spot for Movistar Plus+, part of Telefónica, airing across Spain during the World Cup. For Movistar alone, they generated over 5000 assets (1000 videos) in around 65 iteration rounds, exposing bottlenecks in asset management, collaboration, rendering latency and model consistency. Their serverless architecture uses Cloud Run, Pub/Sub, Cloud Storage, Vertex AI and a Rule of 6 to enable real-time collaboration and cost efficiency. The production team describes the resulting campaign as 95% AI-generated, with 1,441 assets live on a shared Canvas near launch. The spot follows Tommy, a 17-year-old student making an AI video project.
items.title: Mito Orchestrates Thousands of AI Assets for a World Cup TV Spot

items.summary: US payrolls rose by 165,000 in October after a revised September gain of 60,000, the Labor Department’s Bureau of Labour Statistics said on Nov 6. The unemployment rate fell to 4.1% from 4.2%. Reuters economists had forecast gains of 65,000. Professional and business services led with 70,000 jobs added. Average hourly earnings rose 3.1% over the past 12 months, still behind inflation.
items.title: US October Payrolls Beat Forecasts as Unemployment Drops

items.summary: Sony Group introduced a US$60 (S$77) wired headphone model, the MDR-3R, styled after 1979 Walkman-era headphones but updated with USB-C connectivity and an in-line microphone. The company said it kept the original's 23mm drivers for similar sound while adding subtle refinements to suit modern listening.
items.title: Sony Launches Retro-Styled Wired Headphones at $60

items.summary: Databricks presents Unity Gateway as a way for public sector organizations to govern artificial intelligence at scale, building on existing data governance rather than adding separate infrastructure. The piece argues that agencies handle sensitive citizen and defense information, so compliance requirements are mandatory; without answers to cost, access, and where requests are processed, projects stall. It describes how the tool lets teams control which models and agents run for each mission, set spending limits by user or team, apply platform-level content guardrails, route tasks through more cost-effective models via Smart Routing, and require that foundation-model requests be processed within a workspace's geography. Unity Gateway is built into Databricks so administrators can manage access without deploying an external solution.
items.title: Unity Gateway Brings AI Governance To Public Sector

items.summary: US stocks recovered on Wall Street following the market's most severe single-day drop in nearly two years, driven by renewed optimism over a strong jobs report. The Nasdaq rose 1.2% while tech names like Nvidia and AMD led gains; the Dow fell about 1%. European markets had tumbled overnight after Democrats won the midterms, sparking AI-industry slowdown worries.
items.title: Wall Street rebounds after worst day in 19 months amid AI-slowdown fears

items.summary: Feature Views, a capability of Databricks Feature Store, let teams define each ML feature once so the same definition produces point-in-time training data and managed pipelines for online inference. The walkthrough follows a $900 payment through Kafka to a Model Serving endpoint that returns fraud_probability and fraud_prediction. Real-time detection must weigh recent activity, longer-term baselines such as a 30-day average and standard deviation, and the current request amount; one customer's $900 sits six standard deviations above their mean while another's sits only one above theirs. A single definition prevents data leakage from future transactions and training-serving skew between offline scoring and live inference. The design is governed by Unity Catalog for permissions and lineage, with feature privileges controlling registration, reading and materialization.
items.title: Databricks Feature Views unify fraud model training and live scoring

items.summary: Global tech stocks fell sharply following the Democrats' victory in the US midterm elections, with concerns about a slowdown in artificial intelligence development. Major corporations including Apple, Tesla and Nvidia lost around $1tn during one trading session. Reporters question whether this reflects market volatility or signals that an AI bubble may be close to bursting.
items.title: Tech stocks plunge amid fears of AI bubble burst after Democrats' midterms sweep

items.summary: Shares in artificial intelligence and technology firms rose on Friday as markets recovered from a rout that wiped trillions off values, beginning Thursday in the US before spreading to Asia and Europe. Investors had sold AI shares partly over fears that Democrats' control of both houses could slow development through new rules. The Nasdaq Composite flattened around 1.7% higher by lunchtime after its 5.5% fall, while Nvidia gained about 4%. Asian and European markets fared worse, with South Korea's Kospi down 6%. Strong US jobs figures added context: employers added 165,000 jobs in October, above expectations, and unemployment eased to 4.1%, though the rate had held near that range since March. Analysts noted uncertainty over whether the rebound would hold next week.
items.title: AI stocks rebound after midterm-driven tech selloff

items.summary: Investors are weighing whether Democratic control of Congress could burst the AI bubble, after steep falls on world stock markets and a sharp Nasdaq sell-off following mid-term elections that gave Democrats full congressional control. Fears have grown that leading Democrats' campaigns against data-centre expansion will bring more regulation; a Gallup poll in May found 71% would oppose a local data centre versus 53% for a nuclear station. The AI boom, sparked by Open AI's Chat GPT release in late 2022, is expected to reach $1trillion in investments in 2026 alone per Goldman Sachs. Analysts remain divided on whether the drop signals an overvalued market or simply froth being removed.
items.title: US Midterm Wins Spark AI Stock Sell-off

items.summary: In The Vergecast episode titled 'Big Tech lost big in the 2026 election,' Nilay Patel argues that AI products are not good enough to justify their costs. He contends the benefits of features like AI overviews and agents are not real, deep fake content is low quality, data center noise burdens residents, companies spend more than they earn, blood-storage refrigerators in Europe have been hacked, and ties these costs to corruption involving CEOs in Washington.
items.title: Nilay Patel says Big Tech lost big in the 2026 election

items.summary: Obbe Vermeij, a former Rockstar tech director who left in 2009, told Rock Paper Shotgun that an AI-assisted decompilation port of GTA VI could pressure the developer to release its official PC version sooner. He recalled how console fans of the original game resented being given far fewer colors than PC players received. Vermeij noted the long-standing awkward relationship between PC and console releases at Rockstar, where ports often lagged years behind.
items.title: Ex-GTA Tech Director Says AI Clones May Speed Official PC Port

items.summary: An author reports that AI labs are paying companies large one-time fees for copies of their internal work records—emails, documents, chat logs—to train models. Pitches cited include Wired payments reported at $350K–$1.8M and a possible $2 million raise by another emailer; an entrepreneur friend noted spending over $45B on private data. Startups like Handshake license professional documents across fields including journalism and graduate coursework, while Mercor and Micro1 lead the boom. One founder claims labs pay about $40–$50 billion a year for such data. Privacy critics warn anonymization may not fully remove personal information, citing Spirit Airlines’ sale of 80,000 email accounts amid union objections; Google bid $10 million before Micro1 topped it by $2.5 million. The author declined to sell WIRED’s editorial records.
items.title: AI Firms Race to Buy Workers' Private Work Files

items.summary: The International Energy Agency said in its Renewables 2026 report that global renewable capacity is expected to grow by almost 4,800 gigawatts over the 2026-2031 period. The agency attributed faster deployment to energy security concerns and rising fuel prices following a Strait of Hormuz crisis. Emerging markets outside China are set to match advanced economies for the first time.
items.title: IEA Forecasts Nearly 4,800 GW of New Renewables by 2031 Amid Energy Security Push

items.summary: In Edmunds’ EV Range test, the 2027 BMW iX3 50 xDrive drove 436 miles on a single charge, topping its EPA estimate of 392 miles by 44 miles. Powered by an 800V system and a 108.7 kWh battery, it also used less energy than advertised—28.3 vs. 32 kWh per 100 miles. Edmunds calls it the longest-range luxury EV SUV tested so far.
items.title: BMW iX3 Beats Its Own EPA Range Rating in Real-World Test

items.summary: TikTok owner ByteDance is reportedly considering expanding a data center project in northeastern Brazil, according to Bloomberg News. The report was published on Friday and reflects an ongoing evaluation of the company's plans for its Brazilian operations.
items.title: ByteDance Weighs Data Center Expansion in Brazil

items.summary: In the third quarter, Alphabet built a stake worth nearly $548 million in longtime partner Qualcomm as it expands into data centers amid a smartphone downturn. Qualcomm shares rose 3 per cent premarket after tumbles earlier. The chipmaker expects its data-center revenue to reach $15 billion by 2029 and has secured orders from Amazon, Microsoft and Meta.
items.title: Alphabet Builds $548 Million Stake in Qualcomm Amid Data Center Push

items.summary: India's passenger vehicle market shows strong festive demand around Dhanteras and Diwali, with some makers struggling over inventory limits. Maruti Suzuki India expects about 30,000 vehicles on Dhanteras; Hyundai Motor India targets roughly 16,000 across the two days, nearly 14% higher than last year; Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles anticipates single-day deliveries crossing 12,000 units. Mahindra faces tight SUV stocks and capacity constraints as demand outpaces supply.
items.title: Indian automakers forecast strong Dhanteras deliveries amid tight stock

items.summary: OpenAI's chief financial officer Sarah Friar told CNBC on Friday that the company will continue spending on AI computing capacity, even though Tuesday's midterm elections saw voters back limits on data centers in local ballot measures.
items.title: OpenAI CFO Vows Data Center Spending After Election Rebuke

items.summary: Anthropic has introduced a Personal Finance feature that lets users connect their bank and credit card accounts to its AI assistant Claude. The tool answers spending questions in everyday language, breaking down expenses, flagging missed payments, and estimating remaining funds before payday. It analyses financial information only and is not designed to handle money or make investment decisions.
items.title: Anthropic Adds Personal Finance Feature to Claude for Spending Analysis

items.summary: The European Commission launched a WTO safeguard investigation into certain PET resin chemicals, notified under G/SG/N/6/EU/5. The inquiry examines whether increased imports are causing or threatening serious injury to the domestic industry. Interested parties may submit questionnaires within 21 days of initiation and request hearings in the same period; written representations must be filed by the stated deadlines.
items.title: EU launches safeguard investigation into PET resin chemicals

items.summary: A fresh wave of bomb threats disrupted at least 18 flights on Friday, affecting airports and airspace in Bulgaria, Cyprus, Czechia, France, Hungary, Italy, Portugal, Romania and the UK. Searches found no explosive devices and all aircraft landed safely. The alerts followed separate warnings on Tuesday and Thursday that forced at least 35 flights to be diverted or searched, raising questions over an apparently coordinated effort to cause chaos for travellers. Officials described it as a possible hybrid aggression campaign targeting civilian infrastructure, while investigators reported no evidence of state sponsorship.
items.title: Bomb threats disrupt flights across Europe amid coordinated-attack fears

items.summary: The Mission Trinity Foodbank in Goole has closed after 16 years, citing rising costs and falling donations. Founder David Sample said funds had declined to the point where they could no longer afford to continue, worsened by the cost of living crisis. The charity bought food up to three times weekly despite reduced donations and supported about 50-60 families each week until January.
items.title: East Yorkshire foodbank closes after 16 years amid rising costs

items.summary: Senate Democratic leader Catherine Cortez Masto says a wave of new red-state senators will reshape the caucus by uniting moderates and progressives on core priorities like restoring Obamacare tax credits, cutting tariffs, limiting Trump’s power over ICE, and protecting energy jobs. She told Semafor she expects center and left to align in 2027. The influx follows her behind-the-scenes work as chair of ModSquad, which raised $4 million for Democrats and whose associated PAC spent $18 million nationally, including $3. 5 million in Iowa and nearly $5 million backing centrists in Virginia and Colorado. New senators-elect include Josh Turek, Adam Hamilton, Abdul El-Sayed, Roy Cooper, James Talarico, Peggy Flanagan, Troy Jackson, Chris Pappas, Scott Colom, and Juliana Stratton. The new members will not be sworn in until next year, but decisions await during the lame duck session on permitting reform and a potential government funding deal.
items.title: Cortez Masto Sees Red-State Democrats Uniting Party Center and Left

items.summary: Qatar's sovereign wealth fund and Brookfield are backing a proposed 1-gigawatt data center in northern England, potentially the UK's largest. The buildout at Drax Power Station marks Qatar Investment Authority's Qai's first investment from its $20 billion AI infrastructure venture. Partners plan to invest $3.4 billion over five years, though construction still needs approval and an anchor tenant.
items.title: Qatar and Brookfield Back Supersized UK Data Center

items.summary: Elon Musk announced Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production around mid-2027 to make room for the Cybercab robotaxi. The pickup has faced weak sales, with US figures falling 48% in 2025 to 20,237 vehicles per Kelley Blue Book estimates cited by the Associated Press. Musk did not clarify whether production would relocate or end entirely, nor address outstanding orders.
items.title: Tesla Plans Cybertruck Production Wind-Down in 2027

items.summary: The EU's diplomatic position at next week's COP31 summit in Antalya is complicated by a domestic political retreat on climate policy and rising global opposition to its carbon border tax, the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM). India has hardened its stance: Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav said New Delhi will defend industrial interests against what he called unilateral trade barriers, while Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal warned CBAM could raise import duties. The EU's CBAM took effect in January 2026 and covers aluminum, cement, fertilisers, hydrogen, iron and steel. Canada, the United States, the UK and Russia have all sought exemptions or raised disputes, with Russia and China announcing joint opposition on 3 November. Meanwhile, EU co-legislators are set to meet on 20 November as Brussels weighs extending CBAM to washing machines and car parts amid pressure over energy prices and industrial concerns.
items.title: EU Climate Tax Risks Trade War With India at COP31

items.summary: In Mississippi, Democrat Scott Colom leads Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith by about 1,800 votes with roughly 96% of ballots counted. Under state law allowing late mail-in ballots, the Associated Press has not called the contest and a final result may not arrive until early next week.
items.title: Mississippi Senate Race Remains Uncalled as Democrats Chase Blue Wave

items.summary: Chinese scientists aboard China's space station cooled a cloud of rubidium atoms to an equivalent temperature of 9.7 trillionths of a degree above absolute zero, described as a record low by the research team. The result was published in Science and used the ultracold atom physics facility in the Mengtian laboratory module. The reported figure characterizes the atoms' slow expansion rather than any surrounding equipment reaching that temperature. Researchers observed cloud expansion for seven seconds after release, enabling longer experiments into quantum behavior and precision measurements.
items.title: Chinese Scientists Set Atomic Cooling Record on Space Station

items.summary: China launched satellites 07-09 of the Yaogan-51 group from the Xichang Satellite Launch Center in Sichuan Province on November 5, 2026. The launch occurred at 11:58 p.m. Beijing Time aboard a Long March-2C carrier rocket and reached its preset orbits successfully. The satellites are used for scientific experiments and electromagnetic environment detection. This was the 675th mission of the Long March rockets.
items.title: China Launches Yaogan-51 Remote Sensing Satellites

items.summary: On Friday (Nov 6), bomb threats warning 'the clock is ticking' were sent to television stations across Europe, prompting evacuations and suspensions of programming. Irish broadcaster RTE, Britain's Sky, Bulgarian station Nova TV and others reported the alerts; no bombs were found at any site. The emails, signed by a purported leader claiming responsibility for recent flight hoaxes, used the name Mikhail Andropov. Their authorship remains unclear, with uncertainty about possible Russian involvement or an attempt to implicate Moscow.
items.title: Bomb Threat Emails Disrupt European TV Channels Amid Broader Hoax Wave

items.summary: Researchers in Canada captured images of an unidentified baby North Atlantic right whale off Anticosti Island in Quebec in September, one of the rarest sea mammals globally. Scientists with the New England Aquarium in Boston said after analyzing photos and data that it was a calf likely born months ago during winter surveys when the animals went unseen.
items.title: Scientists Identify Baby Right Whale Off Canada

items.summary: European officials reported a fresh wave of bomb threats against multiple flights on Friday, following several hoaxes that caused flight diversions earlier in the week. No suspicious items were found and no one was injured, though authorities noted minimal disruption to aviation across the continent, according to Eurocontrol. The authority said it recorded 14 threatened flights Thursday — only 0.05% of nearly 26,300 daily flights — plus seven on Tuesday. Incidents spanned Hungary, France and Prague's Vaclav Havel Airport, where nine flights were affected. No clear evidence has emerged about who is behind the threats, which come amid warnings that Russia may be ramping up hybrid attacks in Europe. Broadcasters including Ireland's RTE also received security threats.
items.title: Bomb threats target European air traffic amid hoaxes

items.summary: British comedian Russell Brand was found guilty by a London jury on November 5, 2014, of rape and three sexual assaults. The verdict included charges involving a 16-year-old girl. Judge stated he now faces significant prison time.
items.title: Russell Brand Found Guilty of Rape and Three Sexual Assaults

items.summary: A Ukrainian drone team from the 140th Intelligence Battalion of the Ukrainian Marines, led by Snake and including chief pilot Shamil (33), operates the Baton attack drone to contest Russia’s presence on the left bank of the Dnipro River in the Kherson region. The unit launches the craft—costing around $3,300 to produce—from a concealed catapult near trees, steering it live from an underground position while its camera feed goes dark moments before impact. Snake frames the conflict as “a war of drone pilots,” noting that since 2022 Ukraine has shifted from a 20th-century to a 21st-century war. Analyst Petro Kobernyk warns that Russian control of the river could enable further advances into Mykolaiv and Odessa, though he doubts Moscow currently lacks resources for another assault on Kherson.
items.title: Ukrainian drone unit contests Russian hold of the Dnipro

items.summary: A Kenyan High Court in Mombasa sentenced Pastor Paul Mackenzie, leader of the Good News International Church, to 200 years in prison on Friday. He was convicted of murdering 191 people after ordering followers to fast to death. Justice Diana Kavedza found him guilty of relocating members and causing their deaths. Prosecutors sought the death penalty; his lawyer has launched an appeal.
items.title: Kenyan cult leader sentenced to 200 years for mass killings

items.summary: US authorities have charged Thomas Markle, Meghan Markle's father, with possessing child pornography, alleging he kept images of himself with prepubescent girls. FBI agents searched his Florida aged-care home on Friday; he is expected in Tampa court later that day. The Justice Department says the material was stored in two Los Angeles-area units for nearly two decades. First Assistant US Attorney Bill Essayli said they will prosecute to the fullest extent of federal law, and FBI Director Kash Patel confirmed the arrest.
items.title: Meghan Markle's father charged with possessing child pornography

items.summary: In Switzerland, campaigners displayed a 676-square-metre banner near a data centre being developed by STACK Infrastructure. The display showed images of Elon Musk and Jeff Bezos with the slogan 'Big Tech Bros suck our water, electricity, data'. Greenpeace is calling for a nationwide moratorium on new mega data centres until binding regulations protect energy supplies, water resources and public interest.
items.title: Greenpeace Unveils Giant Banner Criticizing Big Tech Data Centres in Switzerland

items.summary: An article examines France's mounting debt costs amid political instability, arguing that planned school and university funding may exceed available resources. Public debt stands at around 120% of GDP, with interest payments projected to rise from €79 billion in 2026 toward between €125 billion and €132 billion by 2030. Economist Friedrich Heinemann warns that rising spreads could trigger a financial crisis unless course correction occurs. Landry Charrier notes many citizens remain insulated from debt consequences, sustaining support for costly party promises. The piece draws on data including Germany's lower ratio and France's negative credit outlook to frame the risk.
items.title: France's Debt Burden and Political Gridlock Threaten Stability

items.summary: Europe is advancing a push for technological sovereignty as artificial intelligence grows, though an AI system built entirely on European technology remains impossible given reliance on U.S. chips from Nvidia alone. The most critical dimension lies in where data is stored and processed; many companies now resist sending sensitive information to the servers of OpenAI, Anthropic, Google or Microsoft. Charles Sansbury, chief executive of Cloudera, notes that businesses increasingly prefer private clouds or local servers. Marjorie Janiewicz of Mistral says enriching models with proprietary data preserves a competitive edge. A Cloudera report based on surveys of more than 1,500 technology leaders worldwide found nearly half have moved part of their AI operations to private systems.
items.title: European Firms Seek Data Control Amid AI Sovereignty Push

items.summary: Professor Steve Tsang of SOAS's China Institute told FRANCE 24 that, while a weakened Trump could strengthen Beijing's negotiating position, the Chinese leadership views Congress as having limited sway over foreign policy and wants to preserve warm personal ties between the two presidents. The item reports that Democrats took control of both chambers.
items.title: China keeps a close eye on US midterm shake-up

items.summary: As the first week of the 2026 Dakar Youth Olympic Games closed, China topped the medal count with nine golds, three silvers and two bronzes. Japan followed in second place on eight golds, while Egypt placed fourth. South Africa had one gold so far, Kenya won its first women's rugby sevens title, Madagascar earned a historic medal, and host Senegal still awaited its second medal.
items.title: China Leads Medal Count at Dakar Youth Olympics After Week One

items.summary: Researchers at Check Point Research found that OpenAI's ChatGPT Lockdown Mode, designed to limit prompt-injection risks and data leaks, contained an escape route. Using HTML previews inside code blocks, they opened unrestricted pop-up windows enabling silent chat-data theft, credential phishing and malware delivery through a trusted interface. Eli Smadja of Check Point Research said AI security controls depend on the surrounding application environment. OpenAI removed the sandbox permissions after disclosure; a retest confirmed the method no longer works.
items.title: Check Point finds vulnerability in ChatGPT’s Lockdown Mode

items.summary:
A Reuters report citing independent researcher Derik Kauffman says Apple keeps an undisclosed multilingual list of roughly 100,000 words that its iPhone keyboard avoids suggesting through predictive text, autocorrect and swipe-typing. Kauffman said most flagged expressions are vulgar or offensive, but the list also excludes politically sensitive phrases about leaders, immigration and territorial disputes, including 'dictator Trump' and 'Tibetan independence.' Apple told Reuters users can still type words manually and override suggestions, describing its keyboard as designed to avoid inappropriate language. Kauffman called it a light-touch form of censorship with large impact at scale, while questioning the filtering's consistency, noting phrases like 'read gay smut' were restricted even when similar ones were not. Reuters independently tested several expressions and found them difficult or impossible to enter via swipe-typing or autocomplete.

items.title: Apple's Hidden Word Filter Draws Scrutiny Over Political and Personal Phrases

items.summary: Shiv Sena minister Sanjay Shirsat alleged on Friday that AIMIM state president Imtiaz Jaleel had been named a prime accused in the Nashik Tata Consultancy Services case involving alleged sexual harassment and religious conversion. Shirsat claimed Jaleel arranged shelter for key accused Nida Khan, who stayed 35 days with relatives, and that voice samples matched recordings linked to the case. Jaleel confirmed being made a co-accused but said he was unaware of the charges; TCS maintained its zero-tolerance policy on harassment.
items.title: Shiv Sena Minister Accuses AIMIM Leader of Sheltering TCS Nashik Case Accused

items.summary: A researcher named Derek Kauffman reported discovering an undisclosed list of roughly 100,000 multilingual terms that Apple's iOS keyboard omits from predictive and swipe-typing features. Reuters said the list contains vulgar, drug-, sex- and violence-related words plus politically sensitive phrases such as 'dictator Trump' and 'sleepy Joe.' Kauffman called it a light-touch censorship whose scale could produce large effects. He estimated around 100,000 entries excluding Chinese characters; Reuters independently corroborated findings with swipe-typing tests on United Ireland and Sleepy Joe.
items.title: Researcher Reveals Apple's Hidden Word Graylist

items.summary: Tribal activist Nisha Kumari Bhagat allegedly died by suicide in Ranchi on Friday, hanging from a ceiling fan at her residence. Police said prima facie she took her own life after going live on Facebook and accusing the Hemant Soren government and land brokers of harassing her; the exact reason is yet to be ascertained. The nearly 11-minute video cuts off with the camera obstructed by a green object.
items.title: Jharkhand tribal activist dies by suicide after Facebook Live

items.summary: Rahul Gandhi, leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha, asked home minister Amit Shah to persuade Prime Minister Narendra Modi to hold a debate on special intensive revision (SIR) of voter rolls. He shared a video showing Shah contradicting his own remarks during parliamentary discussion and urged him not to 'confuse' the prime minister with such statements.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi Urges Shah To Convince Modi For SIR Debate

items.summary: Speculation is growing over a possible power struggle in Maharashtra’s Nationalist Congress Party, which split into two factions in 2023. Nephew Rohit Pawar warned relatives Sunetra Pawar and her sons to understand BJP strategies, while senior leaders reportedly met Union home minister Amit Shah, though the NCP spokesperson Umesh Patil denied it as “completely incorrect.” The buzz follows Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s message of support for hospitalised Sharad Pawar. The party has denied all speculations of any power tussle within the party. Analysts suggest BJP may seek to co-opt Sharad Pawar’s political infrastructure, with possible cabinet gains and opposition realignment at stake.
items.title: NCP Factions Face Possible Political Churn Amid Modi-Pawar Overtures

items.summary: As India and the US work to finalise a long-awaited trade deal, Republicans' loss in the November 3 midterms has raised questions about how the shift affects negotiations. Experts offer differing views: Professor Rituparna Kaushik of FLAME University said results would not rewrite US policy overnight because Section 301 and Section 232 duties rest on executive authority facing a presidential veto, though a Democratic Congress may give India room to negotiate on substance. Ajay Srivastava of the Global Trade Research Initiative expects Trump to fast-track an early agreement amid domestic constraints, yet warned protectionism would remain largely unchanged. For 2025, goods exports reached $103.82 billion from India and about $45.6 billion from the US, with total bilateral trade at $149.42 billion; services trade hit $92.23 billion. A final deal remains elusive amid a Section 301 probe and threats of tariffs around 17-19 per cent linked to Russian oil purchases.
items.title: US midterm losses may reshape India-US trade talks

items.summary: Shares of TD Power and Thermax fell about 15% each, while HFCL and Sterlite Technologies hit the lower circuit on a broad Indian tech rout. The decline followed concerns that Democratic gains in the US midterm elections could restrict data centre expansion and slow AI infrastructure development. A sharp technology sell-off erased roughly $2.5 trillion from US markets, with the Nasdaq Composite dropping 5.52% to close at 24,315, its steepest single-day fall since April 2025. The rout spread across Asia as investors de-risked amid uncertainty over AI spending and valuation resets.
items.title: Indian stocks fall as global AI selloff deepens amid US election fears

items.summary: The Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) released the subject-wise date sheet for its Class 10 and Class 12 board examinations in 2027. Both levels begin on February 16, with all papers starting at 10:30 am; Class 10 ends March 9 and Class 12 concludes April 9. The board said more than 26.5 lakh students registered for Class 10 while over 19.8 lakh are expected in Class 12, and it considered more than 40,000 subject combinations to avoid clashes.
items.title: CBSE Releases Class 10 and 12 Exam Schedule for 2027

items.summary: Professor Amanda Ellison of Durham University, author of Splitting, explains that the appeal of quick fixes for migraines needs evidence before it becomes reliable advice. She describes how prodrome symptoms like yawning and food cravings can make chocolate seem to trigger attacks when it merely reflects an early phase; a review found insufficient evidence to recommend avoiding it. Caffeine has a legitimate place in some headache medicines, per a Cochrane review, though fast-food meals cannot be treated as remedies. Cooling offers short-term relief but not spoon-level certainty. Established options include triptans and CGRP-targeting preventives. She recommends keeping a headache diary to spot patterns rather than assuming unfamiliar symptoms are migraine.
items.title: A neuroscientist weighs which migraine remedies actually work

items.summary: A 15-month-old elephant calf named Maya was airlifted from Kochi Airport in Kerala to Vantara in Jamnagar, Gujarat, for specialised medical care. In July 2026 she suffered an accidental fall and could not stand or rise on her own for nearly two months. After the Kerala Forest Department's treatment failed to improve her condition, a Medical Board recommended shifting her; both teams arranged joint care during the flight so she can receive intensive rehabilitation.
items.title: Kerala elephant calf airlifted for specialised care at Vantara

items.summary: Bhavya Dore reviews Abir Mukherjee's novel The Pinnacle, noting it is his eighth book and the second set in a contemporary setting. George Abercrombie, an American star living in Mumbai, becomes the prime suspect after discovering his wife Sweety Sahota murdered in their luxury high-rise apartment. Published by Harvill Secker at 432 pages for Rs.899, the novel rotates between three points of view and blends intrigue with comedy. Dore praises Mukherjee's trademark drollery but flags historical inaccuracies that undermine verisimilitude before calling it a fun, solid thriller.
items.title: A Reviewer Frames Abir Mukherjee's Mumbai Thriller
